findings.ref: specs/epic-194-a6-lite-integration/verification/qg/shared/regression.log, 2026-08-25 second-pass section ('THIS FEATURE'S OWN SUITES, both runtimes, with byte-identical assertion labels between twins'); verification/T-002.green.log TEST-013r lines in the .sh and .ps1 sections; tests/check-ri[REDACTED].tests.ps1 TEST-013r assertion; risk-upgrade-policy.md '## Input and result contract'
findings.note: The byte-identical-assertion-labels claim is falsified by the green log it cites: TEST-013r reads 'hits the primary-source-unavailable arm (exit 2)' in the sh twin and 'is rejected (exit 1)' in the ps1 twin, and every TEST-013 sh label carries a trailing '(not the input-unavailable one)' clause the ps1 twin drops. The substance behind the label difference is a real cross-runtime divergence: for the identical bare two-positional invocation the sh SUT returns the documented exit 2 with 'risk-upgrade: input unavailable' while the ps1 SUT returns exit 1 with a PowerShell parameter-binding error, outside the 0/2/10 exit contract risk-upgrade-policy.md documents, and the ps1 assertion is deliberately loose (exit -ne 0 -and -ne 10) so it cannot detect it. It appears pre-existing rather than introduced by T-002, so AC-007's live-versus-SUT byte identity is unaffected; the defect is the overstated parity claim in the evidence.

findings.ref: human-copy/plugins/sdd-lite/scripts/check-risk-upgrade.sh (entry.get('upgrade_reasons') or [] then the isinstance list check) and check-risk-upgrade.ps1 (Test-PythonFalsy guarding the -isnot [array] branch); requirements.md Field Definitions 'Capability-derived trigger fragment' and AC-027; risk-upgrade-policy.md exit-2 enumeration
findings.note: AC-027 requires a supplied shape-invalid fragment to exit 2, and Field Definitions type upgrade_reasons as an array. Both twins deliberately treat a falsy-but-present non-array value (false, 0, empty string) as absent, so a fragment entry {id: x, eligible: false, upgrade_reasons: false} exits 10 with triggers=ineligible:x instead of exiting 2, while a truthy non-array (TEST-013i) exits 2. The two runtimes agree and the outcome still Blocks, so this is fail-closed in effect rather than a fail-open, but the asymmetry appears in neither risk-upgrade-policy.md's exit-2 enumeration nor any assertion in the four suites.
